clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced himself from your mother; your uncle Anton began drinking at lunch with a warning at work; your uncle separated from Celeste; your mother lay awake over them; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. By May 1979 your grandmother had taken a job at the library and was out of the house every day, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984–1984
clusters.reason: Around March 1984 when your mother was ordered to bed for the rest of her pregnancy, within months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house; your father argued with her over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. In September your sister Ines was born and the shifts settled. Two shifts count; they fit together as reactions in the household around your mother's loss of functioning and your grandmother's move into the daily care.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, over the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news of her; Hazel had a bad fall and walked with a frame; she steadied on a new medicine; your father and uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather's chest pains began; Hazel could no longer dress herself; your mother took her to the clinic twice a week; your aunt Mavis came one week in four to nurse her sister; your father drank most evenings; your aunt Pearl had panic spells at the wheel; Hazel had a good summer and then could no longer stand; your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side; and your father fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house. In June 1997 Hazel moved to the Fairlie nursing home and your father cut his drinking back to weekends by October, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around May 1999 when your brother Callum left home for a job at the mines up north, within the year: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere, even to work; and by August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and had passed her exams, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within months: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you stopped returning your mother's calls; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark. By November you had taken a job at the garden centre and were sleeping through the night again, and the shifts settled. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
